questions.question: Mukund has two grandsons Sachin and Chetan. 13 year old Sachin gets some money from Mukund’s wealth and 14 year old Chetan gets rest of the money. But Sachin and Chetan will get money only when they turn 23 years old. Till then the money is in a bank getting interest at rate 10% compounded annually. When both turn 23, they receive the same amount. How much had Mukund given Chetan (in ₹) initially, if total money with Mukund was ₹25200?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Time difference for Sachin (23 − 13 = 10 yrs) and Chetan (23 − 14 = 9 yrs) is 1 year.

When compound amounts are equal, the principal ratio is inversely proportional to the accumulating factor (1 + R/100)T.

Ratio of Chetan's share to Sachin's share = (1 + 10/100)¹ : 1 = 11 : 10.

Chetan's share = 11 / (11 + 10) × 25200 = (11 / 21) × 25200 = 13200.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total money = ₹25200

Sachin's age = 13 years, Chetan's age = 14 years

Time for Sachin (T₁) = 23 − 13 = 10 years

Time for Chetan (T₂) = 23 − 14 = 9 years

Rate of Interest (R) = 10% compounded annually

**Formula Used:**

Amount in Compound Interest = P × (1 + R/100)T

questions.question: Two trains are moving in opposite directions at speeds of 140 km/h and 80 km/h. The length of one train is 340 m. The time taken by them to cross each other is 11 seconds. The length (in m) of the other train, correct to 2 decimal places, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed of trains in opposite directions = 140 + 80 = 220 km/h.

Convert speed to m/s: 220 × (5/18) = 1100/18 m/s.

Total distance covered = Speed × Time = (1100/18) × 11 = 12100/18 ≈ 672.22 m.

Length of the second train = Total distance − Length of first train = 672.22 − 340 = 332.22 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 332.22 m.**

questions.question: Find the effective discount for the scheme 'buy 10, get 6 free'.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 'Buy X Get Y Free' schemes, the discount percentage is calculated on the total items given.

Discount % = [Free items ÷ (Buy items + Free items)] × 100

Discount % = [6 ÷ (10 + 6)] × 100

Discount % = (6 ÷ 16) × 100 = 37.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Items bought (paid for) = 10

Free items received = 6

**Formula Used:**

Discount % = (Total Discount ÷ Total Marked Price) × 100

 
 
 10 Paid Items
 
 
 
 6 Free Items

 
 

 Customer Pays For (SP)

 
 

 Discount

 
 

 Total 16 Items (Total MP)

 
 Discount % = (6 ÷ 16) × 100 = 37.5%

**Calculations:**

Let the Marked Price (MP) of 1 item be 1 unit.

⇒ Total items taken by customer = 10 (bought) + 6 (free) = 16 items

⇒ Total MP of 16 items = 16 units

⇒ Selling Price (SP) paid by customer = MP of 10 items = 10 units

⇒ Discount given = Total MP − SP = 16 − 10 = 6 units

⇒ Discount % = (6 ÷ 16) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (3 ÷ 8) × 100 = 37.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two consecutive discounts of a% and b% are given on an item, the effective discount percentage is given by (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Markup and Discount Relation

Selling Price (SP) can be calculated using both the Cost Price and the Marked Price: SP = CP × (1 + Profit%) = MP × (1 − Discount%).

Dishonest Dealer (False Weight)

If a dealer claims to sell goods at Cost Price but uses a false weight, the true Profit % = [(True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight] × 100.
</p

questions.question: The price (per litre) of petrol increases by 40%. By what percent should its consumption be reduced such that the expenditure on it increases by 12% only?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Required percentage reduction = (Change in Price − Change in Expenditure) ÷ (100 + Change in Price) × 100

⇒ % Reduction = (40 − 12) ÷ (100 + 40) × 100

⇒ % Reduction = 28 ÷ 140 × 100

⇒ % Reduction = 1 ÷ 5 × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

**Given:**

Percentage increase in petrol price = 40%

Percentage increase in expenditure = 12%

**Formula Used:**

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

questions.question: A vendor bought 120 shirts at the rate of ₹375 per shirt and sold them for ₹48,600. What is his gain/loss percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price (SP) of 1 shirt = 48600 ÷ 120 = ₹405

Ratio of Cost Price (CP) to SP = 375 : 405 = 25 : 27

Gain = 2 parts on a base of 25 parts

Gain % = (2 ÷ 25) × 100 = 8%

**∴ The correct answer is Gain 8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of shirts = 120

Cost Price (CP) of 1 shirt = ₹375

Total Selling Price (SP) = ₹48,600

**Formula Used:**

Profit = Total SP − Total CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

 
 Total CP = ₹45,000
 
 
 Total SP = ₹48,600
 
 
• 
 

 
 Profit = ₹3,600
 + 8%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Cost Price (CP) = 120 × 375 = ₹45,000

⇒ Profit = Total SP − Total CP

⇒ Profit = 48,600 − 45,000 = ₹3,600

⇒ Profit % = (3600 ÷ 45000) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (36 ÷ 450) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 8%

**∴ The correct answer is Gain 8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of an item. Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is given by the formula (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer

If a dealer professes to sell his goods at the Cost Price but uses a false weight, his Profit % = (Error ÷ (True Value − Error)) × 100.

questions.question: The greatest number, which divides 711 and 1040 to leave 48 and 20 respectively as remainders, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Subtract the remainders from the given numbers directly to get exactly divisible numbers:

First number = 711 − 48 = 663

Second number = 1040 − 20 = 1020

The required greatest number is the HCF of 663 and 1020.

The HCF must be a factor of their difference (1020 − 663 = 357). From the options, only 51 is a factor of 357 and divides both 663 and 1020 perfectly.

**∴ The correct answer is 51.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 711 and 1040.

The respective remainders are 48 and 20.

**Formula Used:**

Required Number = HCF of (First Number − Remainder 1) and (Second Number − Remainder 2)

**Calculations:**

⇒ First exact divisible number = 711 − 48 = 663

⇒ Second exact divisible number = 1040 − 20 = 1020

⇒ Prime factorization of 663 = 3 × 13 × 17

⇒ Prime factorization of 1020 = 2² × 3 × 5 × 17

⇒ The common prime factors of 663 and 1020 are 3 and 17

⇒ HCF(663, 1020) = 3 × 17 = 51

**∴ The correct answer is 51.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Greatest Dividing Number (Different Remainders)

To find the greatest number that divides x, y, and z leaving remainders a, b, and c respectively, calculate the HCF of (x − a), (y − b), and (z − c).

Greatest Dividing Number (Same Remainder)

To find the greatest number that divides x, y, and z leaving the same remainder in each case, calculate the HCF of |x − y|, |y − z|, and |z − x|.

Product Rule for HCF & LCM

For any two given numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).
</p

questions.question: To complete a task in 8 days, 10 men or 15 women are required. If 'x' men and 'y' women are needed to complete the same task in 12 days, which of the following equations is correct?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

10 Men = 15 Women ⇒ Efficiency ratio (Man : Woman) = 15 : 10 = 3 : 2.

Let efficiency of 1 man be 3 units/day and 1 woman be 2 units/day.

Total Work = 10 × 3 × 8 = 240 units.

Required efficiency for completing work in 12 days = 240 ÷ 12 = 20 units/day.

Combined efficiency of x men and y women = 3x + 2y.

**∴ The correct answer is 3x+2y=20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ 10 men can complete the task in 8 days.

⇒ 15 women can complete the task in 8 days.

⇒ Time taken by 1 man alone = 10 × 8 = 80 days.

⇒ Time taken by 1 woman alone = 15 × 8 = 120 days.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total assumed work = 240 units.

⇒ The task needs to be completed in 12 days by x men and y women.

⇒ Total efficiency required per day = Total Work ÷ Days

⇒ Required combined efficiency = 240 ÷ 12 = 20 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of x men = 3 × x = 3x.

⇒ Efficiency of y women = 2 × y = 2y.

⇒ Total combined efficiency = 3x + 2y.

⇒ Equating required efficiency with actual efficiency: 3x + 2y = 20.

**∴ The correct answer is 3x+2y=20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Time and Work Concept

Total work is always proportional to the combined efficiency and the time taken. Formula: Total Work = Total Efficiency × Time.

MDH Rule (Chain Rule)

It relates the number of men, days, hours, and work directly. Formula: M₁ × D₁ × H₁ ÷ W₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂ ÷ W₂.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed strictly in proportion to the total actual work completed or the direct ratio of their individual efficiencies.
</p

questions.question: If the three sections of the ninth grade have 30, 45, and 50 students respectively, and their average scores are 80, 75, and 90 respectively, then what is the average score of all the students in the ninth grade?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of number of students in the three sections = 30 : 45 : 50 = 6 : 9 : 10 (Total 25 parts).

Let the assumed average score be 80.

Net deviation = (0 × 6) + (−5 × 9) + (+10 × 10) = 0 − 45 + 100 = +55.

Average deviation = +55 ÷ 25 = +2.2.

Actual average score = 80 + 2.2 = 82.2.

**∴ The correct answer is 82.2 marks.**

questions.question: A person plans to travel a total distance of 60 km in 6 hours, partly on foot and partly by bicycle. His walking speed is 6 km/hr, and his cycling speed is 12 km/hr. What distance (in km) does he cover on foot?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the Alligation method on speed to find the ratio of time taken:

Average speed of the total journey = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 km/hr.

Ratio of time (Walking : Cycling) = (12 − 10) : (10 − 6) = 2 : 4 = 1 : 2.

Time spent on walking = [1 ÷ (1 + 2)] × 6 = 2 hours.

Distance covered on foot = Walking Speed × Walking Time = 6 × 2 = 12 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 60 km

Total time taken = 6 hours

Walking speed = 6 km/hr

Cycling speed = 12 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

questions.question: x and y are directly proportional. If x = 3 when y = 5, then find the value of y when x = 7.8.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since x and y are directly proportional, their ratio y/x remains constant.

Constant ratio = 5 / 3

New value of y = New x × (5 / 3)

New y = 7.8 × (5 / 3) = 2.6 × 5 = 13

**∴ The correct answer is 13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial condition: x₁ = 3, y₁ = 5

New condition: x₂ = 7.8

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 Condition 1
 x = 3
 y = 5
 
 

 × 2.6

 

 × 2.6

 
 Condition 2
 x = 7.8
 y = ?

**Formula Used:**

When two quantities x and y are directly proportional, their ratio is constant: x₁ / y₁ = x₂ / y₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3 / 5 = 7.8 / y₂

⇒ y₂ = (5 × 7.8) / 3

⇒ y₂ = 39 / 3

⇒ y₂ = 13

**∴ The correct answer is 13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportion

When two variables change in the same ratio, they are in direct proportion. The formula used is x₁ / y₁ = x₂ / y₂.

Inverse Proportion

When an increase in one variable leads to a proportional decrease in the other, they are inversely proportional. The formula used is x₁ × y₁ = x₂ × y₂.

Means and Extremes Rule

For any proportion given as a : b :: c : d, the product of the means equals the product of the extremes: b × c = a × d.
</p

questions.question: The average weight of Akshay, Atul and Baban is 46 kg. If the average weight of Akshay and Atul be 39 kg and that of Atul and Baban be 46 kg, then the weight of Atul (in kg) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In overlapping average questions, the value of the overlapping entity is given directly by:

Value = (Sum of group 1) + (Sum of group 2) − (Total Sum)

Atul's weight = (39 × 2) + (46 × 2) − (46 × 3)

Atul's weight = 78 + 92 − 138 = 170 − 138 = 32 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 32 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of Akshay, Atul, and Baban = 46 kg

Average weight of Akshay and Atul = 39 kg

Average weight of Atul and Baban = 46 kg

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

 
 Akshay + Atul + Baban = 138 kg
 
 
 Akshay + Atul = 78 kg
 
 
 Atul + Baban = 92 kg

 

 

 Overlap = Atul

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of Akshay, Atul, and Baban = 46 × 3 = 138 kg

⇒ Total weight of Akshay and Atul = 39 × 2 = 78 kg

⇒ Total weight of Atul and Baban = 46 × 2 = 92 kg

⇒ Sum of weights of both groups = 78 + 92 = 170 kg

⇒ In the sum of both groups, Atul is counted twice (Akshay + Atul + Atul + Baban = 170 kg)

⇒ Weight of Atul = (Sum of both groups) − (Total weight of all three)

⇒ Weight of Atul = 170 − 138 = 32 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 32 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Overlapping Averages

When a specific entity is included in two separate overlapping groups, its individual value is found by: Overlapping Value = (Sum of Group 1) + (Sum of Group 2) − (Total Sum of All).

Average Formula

Average is the arithmetic mean, given by Average = (Sum of observations) ÷ (Total number of observations). Thus, total value is determined by cross-multiplying average and the number of subjects.

Combined Average

If two distinct groups of size n₁ and n₂ have averages A₁ and A₂ respectively, their combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).
</p

questions.question: Find the area (in cm²) of the card board that is required to make a box of size 12 cm × 14 cm × 8 cm.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The area of the cardboard required is equal to the Total Surface Area (TSA) of the box.

TSA = 2 × (lb + bh + hl)

⇒ Area = 2 × (12 × 14 + 14 × 8 + 8 × 12)

⇒ Area = 2 × (168 + 112 + 96)

⇒ Area = 2 × 376 = 752 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 752 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

 Dimensions of the Box

**Given:**

Length (l) = 12 cm

Breadth (b) = 14 cm

Height (h) = 8 cm

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area of a cuboid = 2 × (lb + bh + hl)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of cardboard = 2 × (12 × 14 + 14 × 8 + 8 × 12)

⇒ Area of cardboard = 2 × (168 + 112 + 96)

⇒ Area of cardboard = 2 × 376

⇒ Area of cardboard = 752 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 752 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cuboid

The total space occupied by the cuboid is calculated as Volume = l × b × h.

Lateral Surface Area (LSA)

The area of the four walls of a cuboid, excluding top and bottom, is given by LSA = 2h(l + b).

Length of Diagonal

The longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid is its diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²).

Surface Area of a Cube

For a cube with all sides equal to 'a', the Total Surface Area = 6a² and Lateral Surface Area = 4a².
</p

questions.question: Mandar bought a calculator and sold it to Ketan at a 5% profit. Ketan then sold it to Tushar at a 25% loss. If Tushar bought it for Rs. 3780, what was the cost price (in rupees) of the calculator that Mandar bought?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By applying successive fraction multipliers to the initial price:

Final Price = Initial Price × (100 + Profit%)/100 × (100 − Loss%)/100

3780 = Mandar's CP × (105/100) × (75/100)

3780 = Mandar's CP × (21/20) × (3/4) = Mandar's CP × (63/80)

Mandar's CP = 3780 × (80/63) = 60 × 80 = 4800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Tushar's cost price = ₹3780

Profit percentage for Mandar = 5%

Loss percentage for Ketan = 25%

**Method: Successive Percentage Change**

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

 
 Mandar
 CP = x

 
 Ketan
 CP = 1.05x

 
 Tushar
 ₹3780

 

 

 +5% Profit
 -25% Loss

**Calculations:**

⇒ 5% profit fractional equivalent = + 1/20

⇒ Multiplier for Mandar's Selling Price = (1 + 1/20) = 21/20

⇒ 25% loss fractional equivalent = − 1/4

⇒ Multiplier for Ketan's Selling Price = (1 − 1/4) = 3/4

⇒ Let Mandar's original Cost Price be x.

⇒ Ketan's Cost Price = x × (21/20)

⇒ Tushar's Cost Price = x × (21/20) × (3/4)

⇒ x × (63/80) = 3780

⇒ x = 3780 × (80/63)

⇒ x = 60 × 80 = 4800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Profit and Loss

When an item is sold through a chain of multiple buyers, the final Selling Price = Initial Cost Price × (1 ± P₁/100) × (1 ± P₂/100). We use plus for a profit and minus for a loss.

Equivalent Percentage Change

The overall net percentage change for two successive changes of a% and b% is given by the formula: Net % Change = a + b + (a × b)/100.

5f:T6a

questions.question: Amit invests a sum of ₹5400 and Gopal invests a sum of ₹10200 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 4 years, Gopal gets ₹960 more interest than Amit, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in Principal = ₹10200 − ₹5400 = ₹4800

Simple interest generated by extra principal in 4 years = ₹960

Simple interest for 1 year = 960 ÷ 4 = ₹240

Rate of Interest (R) = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Extra Principal) × 100

R = (240 ÷ 4800) × 100 = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is Principal, R is Rate of Interest, and T is Time.

questions.question: Ashok has ₹1612 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Raj and Varun and asked them to invest it at 8% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Raj and Varun got same amount after 16 and 17 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Ashok give to Raj?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate = 8% = 8/100 = 2/25 ⇒ Multiplying Factor = (1 + 2/25) = 27/25

Time difference = 17 − 16 = 1 year.

To get the same amount, the person with less time needs a larger initial sum.

Ratio of their initial investments (Raj : Varun) = (27)¹ : (25)¹ = 27 : 25

Raj's share = [27 ÷ (27 + 25)] × 1612 = (27 ÷ 52) × 1612 = 27 × 31 = ₹837.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹837.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Principal = ₹1612

Rate of Interest (R) = 8% compounded annually

Time for Raj (T₁) = 16 years

Time for Varun (T₂) = 17 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount in Compound Interest: A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

 Total Principal = ₹1612

 
 Raj: ₹x

 

 16 years @ 8% CI

 
 Amount (A)

 
 Varun: ₹V

 Amount (A)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the principal given to Raj be ₹x.

⇒ Then, the principal given to Varun = ₹(1612 − x).

⇒ According to the given condition, amounts after their respective periods are equal.

⇒ x(1 + 8/100)¹⁶ = (1612 − x)(1 + 8/100)¹⁷

⇒ x = (1612 − x)(1 + 8/100)¹⁷ − ¹⁶

⇒ x = (1612 − x)(1 + 2/25)

⇒ x = (1612 − x)(27/25)

⇒ 25x = 27(1612 − x)

⇒ 25x = 43524 − 27x

⇒ 52x = 43524

⇒ x = 43524 ÷ 52 = 837

**∴ The correct answer is ₹837.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Division of Amount at CI

If a total sum P is divided into parts P₁ and P₂ for n₁ and n₂ years respectively yielding equal amounts, their ratio is P₁/P₂ = (1 + R/100)ⁿ² − ⁿ¹.

Difference Between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on a principal P at rate R% is given directly by Difference = P(R/100)².

Compound Interest Formula (Half-Yearly)

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate is halved and the time is doubled. Amount A = P(1 + R/200)²ⁿ.

Rule of 72

A popular trick to estimate the number of years required to double an investment at a given annual compound interest rate R%. Years ≈ 72 ÷ R.

questions.question: Compare the ratios 12 : 13, 7 : 8, 9 : 10, and 5 : 6. Which one is greater than 0.9 but smaller than 0.95?

Convert the target bounds into fractions with a difference of 1 between the numerator and denominator: 0.9 = 9/10 and 0.95 = 19/20.

For proper fractions where the difference between numerator and denominator is the same, the fraction with larger numerical terms is strictly greater.

Thus, we need a fraction whose values lie strictly between the bounds (9, 10) and (19, 20).

Among the given options, 12/13 is the only fraction satisfying the condition 9 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Comparing Fractions with Equal Differences

If the difference between the numerator and denominator remains constant for proper fractions, the fraction with larger numerical values is fundamentally greater. For example, maintaining a difference of 1 yields the sequence: 5/6 b×c, then a/b is strictly greater than c/d. For instance, comparing 12/13 and 9/10: 12×10 (120) > 13×9 (117) conclusively proves 12/13 > 9/10.

Percentage Conversion Shortcut

Multiplying a ratio's decimal form by 100 transforms it directly into a percentage. The given target boundary of 0.9 to 0.95 naturally translates to 90% to 95%. Since the fraction 12:13 equates to roughly 92.3%, it clearly falls within this designated target bracket.

questions.question: If 4% of x = 120, then x is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Base × Multiplying Factor = Percentage Value

⇒ 4% corresponds to 120.

⇒ 1% corresponds to 120 ÷ 4 = 30.

⇒ 100% corresponds to 30 × 100 = 3000.

**∴ The correct answer is 3000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

4% of x = 120

**Formula Used:**

Value = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Base

**Calculation:**

⇒ (4 ÷ 100) × x = 120

⇒ x = 120 × (100 ÷ 4)

⇒ x = 30 × 100

⇒ x = 3000

**∴ The correct answer is 3000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Base Value in Percentage

In any percentage calculation, the original or total quantity represents the 100% base mark. When given a partial percentage value, solving for the entire base reveals the 100% amount.

Fraction Equivalents

Calculating 4% is mathematically equivalent to dividing the value by 25, since 4% = 4 ÷ 100 = 1/25. Thus, (1/25) × x = 120 directly leads to x = 120 × 25.

Direct Multiplier Method

If p% of a given number is N, the entire number can be quickly deduced using the straightforward transposition formula: Base = N × (100 ÷ p).
